issues.description: Method getTotalNumberOfStudents(): The problem statement (UML) declares +getTotalNumberOfStudents(): int (problem_statement.md line 70) and the exercise text/instructions expect an int total (hint references the UML). The solution implementation (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java) defines public StudentCount getTotalNumberOfStudents() (signature at line 75) and introduces a StudentCount class (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/StudentCount.java, class at line 3). The template (template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java) contains a TODO for this method (line 12) and does not provide a StudentCount type. This mismatch between the UML/text (int) and the solution (StudentCount) will cause confusion and/or compilation issues for students following the problem statement or implementing the method as an int.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the return type consistent across artifacts. Option A (preferable for minimal change): change the solution's getTotalNumberOfStudents() to return an int (sum of numberOfInscribedStudents and numberOfGuestStudents) and remove StudentCount usage from the Lecture solution (or keep StudentCount as an internal helper but do not expose it in the public API). Update solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java accordingly. Option B: if a custom StudentCount wrapper is intended, update the problem statement UML and textual tasks to declare getTotalNumberOfStudents(): StudentCount, and add StudentCount.java to the template_repository (src/de/tum/cit/ase/StudentCount.java) and document its API in the problem text so students can compile and use it. Ensure template and tests reflect the chosen return type so students are not blocked by a type mismatch.

issues.description: The concept 'total number of students' is named inconsistently across artifacts. The problem statement UML and task text refer to a method getTotalNumberOfStudents() that returns a primitive int. The template Lecture.java contains a TODO for adding getTotalNumberOfStudents but provides no implementation. The solution Lecture.java implements getTotalNumberOfStudents() with the signature public StudentCount getTotalNumberOfStudents(), returning an instance of a StudentCount class (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/StudentCount.java) instead of an int. This introduces a new identifier (StudentCount) not mentioned in the problem statement or UML and forces consumers to call getValue() on the returned object to obtain the primitive count, which is not documented in the exercise. Students following the UML/problem will expect an int and may be confused or blocked by the unexpected wrapper type and the additional StudentCount API.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the return type and naming so the conceptual entity 'total number of students' is consistent. Option A (recommended for minimal change to problem): change the solution method to public int getTotalNumberOfStudents() and return numberOfInscribedStudents + numberOfGuestStudents; remove or keep StudentCount only as an internal helper if needed. Option B (if StudentCount is intended): update the problem statement and UML to declare getTotalNumberOfStudents(): StudentCount and document the StudentCount class and its getValue() method in the task description and template so students know to use getValue() to obtain the primitive value. Ensure the template Lecture.java TODOs and any tests reflect the chosen approach.
